city.caveat: This is the official city record as kept, without adjustments. It joins several observing sites over the years, and a move, a new instrument or the city growing around a station can shift readings (city growth mostly warms nights); NOAA's adjusted climate datasets correct for these. Treat any single number as approximate.

text.lede: Yesterday's high of 47°F was the 23rd coolest November 13 high (tied) of 156 since 1871, the coolest since 2022.
text.p_yest: The high of 47°F was the 23rd coolest November 13 high (tied) of 156 since 1871, the coolest since 2022. The normal high for the date is 60°F, and the record is 78°F (1879). The low of 41°F was typical for November 13.
text.t_rec: Knoxville has nearly stopped setting record lows
text.p_rec: If Knoxville's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Knoxville has set 21 standing record lows, far fewer than the 63 that chance alone would give, and 87 record highs, more than the 63 that chance alone would give. The 1930s hold the most record highs of any decade (50). Knoxville's all-time high is 105°F, on June 30, 2012.
text.t_chg: Knoxville's days and nights both warmed. Days warmed faster.
text.p_chg: Across 155 complete years: Knoxville's average low has risen +0.05°F per decade (95% range +0.00 to +0.10), about +0.8°F since 1871. Knoxville's average high has risen +0.17°F per decade (95% range +0.12 to +0.21), about +2.6°F since 1871.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in 2 of 12 months. Highs rose in 10 of 12 months.
text.t_rain: Rain and snow: no clear long-term change
text.p_rain: Knoxville's yearly precipitation shows no clear long-term change (+0.10 inches per decade, a range that includes zero). The 1991–2020 normal is 51.9 inches a year. The wettest year was 1875 (73.77 in); the driest, 1986 (32.48 in).
